subsystems.name: Sensing layer
subsystems.role: captures real-time physical data from machines, processes and products.

subsystems.name: Connectivity and edge
subsystems.role: moves data reliably inside the factory and pre-processes it close to the source.

subsystems.name: Data platform
subsystems.role: stores and organises high-volume, high-frequency data for analysis.

subsystems.name: AI and analytics
subsystems.role: turns data into predictions, classifications and optimised setpoints.
parts: anomaly detection and predictive maintenance models

subsystems.name: Digital twin
subsystems.role: a virtual replica used to simulate changes before applying them to the physical line.

subsystems.name: Control and automation
subsystems.role: executes AI decisions on the factory floor.

subsystems.name: Human interface
subsystems.role: presents insights and allows operators to supervise and intervene.

buildSteps.title: Map processes and choose targets
buildSteps.detail: Identify the lines, machines and metrics where downtime, quality or energy use can be improved; set measurable goals.

buildSteps.title: Instrument the factory
buildSteps.detail: Retrofit or install sensors, cameras and PLCs. Sample vibration at kilohertz rates and temperatures at slower intervals, depending on the failure mode.

buildSteps.title: Build connectivity and edge
buildSteps.detail: Lay industrial Ethernet or private 5G, install edge gateways, and set up protocol translation (e.g. OPC UA) so data can leave legacy machines.

buildSteps.title: Create the data platform
buildSteps.detail: Stream data into a time-series database and data lake; add metadata so each reading is linked to a machine, batch and timestamp.

buildSteps.title: Train AI models
buildSteps.detail: Use historical failure and quality data to train predictive maintenance and optimisation models; validate them against held-out data.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with control
buildSteps.detail: Connect model outputs to MES and SCADA so the system can recommend or automatically adjust speeds, feeds and schedules.

buildSteps.title: Deploy a digital twin
buildSteps.detail: Build a simulation of the line using CAD and physics models, feed it live data, and test changes virtually before rollout.

buildSteps.title: Roll out dashboards and train staff
buildSteps.detail: Give operators and engineers clear interfaces; train them to trust and override the system.

buildSteps.title: Operate and retrain
buildSteps.detail: Monitor model drift, collect new data, and periodically retrain to keep predictions accurate as equipment ages.

prerequisites.why: they provide the raw data on vibration, temperature, flow and position that every model needs.
5G and TSN are still being deployed in factories; many sites rely on older fieldbus systems.
edge servers handle millisecond control, while cloud or on-prem clusters train large models.
supervised and reinforcement learning methods can predict failures and tune setpoints.
connecting legacy machines to networks expands the attack surface, and standards are still maturing.
accurate physics models of whole factories remain costly to build and maintain.

pathway.milestone: wide deployment of condition monitoring and predictive maintenance on critical machines
pathway.unlocks: fewer unplanned stoppages and lower maintenance cost.

pathway.milestone: closed-loop optimisation where AI adjusts process parameters in real time
pathway.unlocks: higher yield and lower energy use per unit.

pathway.milestone: autonomous material handling and scheduling across whole lines
pathway.unlocks: factories that run with minimal human intervention.

pathway.milestone: self-optimising supply networks that negotiate orders between plants
